fullPassage: In the early 1960s the great American writer James Baldwin wrote: “People are trapped in history, and history is trapped in them.” He was speaking to race when he penned those words. But the statement is equally true if the word “people” is replaced with “all of life on Earth, present and past,” for each strand of DNA, in each of our cells, is an ancient record of biological history, written in simple code and passed down from generation to generation. One could say that DNA is nothing but history, one with a physical manifestation that was slowly blended and accumulated over countless eons by the most pitiless of all phenomena — natural selection. DNA is a history that is inside us — and yet one that is our master as well, the blueprint for our bodies, and dictator of what we will pass on to our children, gifts that can be blessings — or deadly time bombs. We are indeed trapped in this particular vehicle of history as much as it is trapped in us.

questions.passage: “People are (A) in history, and history is trapped in them.” Each strand of DNA is an (B) record of biological history. DNA was slowly blended by the most (C) of all phenomena — natural selection.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 갇혀있다(trapped), 고대의(ancient) 기록, 무자비한(pitiless) 자연선택.
det.analysis:
✅ ① trapped — ancient — pitiless: 원문과 일치
❌ ② freed: trapped의 반의어
❌ ③ modern: ancient의 반의어
❌ ④ merciful: pitiless의 반의어
❌ ⑤ 세 단어 모두 불일치

questions.passage: DNA is history with a physical (A) that was slowly accumulated. DNA is our master, the (B) for our bodies, gifts that can be (C) — or deadly time bombs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 물리적 구현(manifestation), 청사진(blueprint), 축복(blessings).
det.analysis:
✅ ① manifestation — blueprint — blessings: 원문과 일치
❌ ② illustration: manifestation과 다름
❌ ③ photograph: blueprint와 다름
❌ ④ curses: blessings의 반의어
❌ ⑤ 세 단어 모두 불일치

questions.passage: People are <u>① trapped</u> in history. Each strand of DNA is an <u>② ancient</u> record. DNA was blended by the most <u>③ pitiless</u> of all phenomena. DNA is the blueprint for our bodies and dictator of what we will pass on, gifts that can be <u>④ trivial</u> — or deadly time bombs. We are indeed trapped in this particular <u>⑤ vehicle</u> of history.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ trivial → blessings: 축복(blessings)이 될 수도 있고 치명적 시한폭탄이 될 수도 있다는 문맥에서 trivial(사소한)은 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① trapped: 갇혀있다, 적절
✅ ② ancient: 고대의, 적절
✅ ③ pitiless: 무자비한, 적절
❌ ④ trivial(사소한) → blessings(축복): 문맥 불일치
✅ ⑤ vehicle: 운반수단, 적절

questions.passage: He was speaking to race when he <u>① penned</u> those words. The statement is true if “people” is <u>② replaced</u> with “all of life on Earth.” DNA was slowly blended and <u>③ destroyed</u> over countless eons. DNA is our master, the <u>④ blueprint</u> for our bodies, and <u>⑤ dictator</u> of what we will pass on.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ destroyed → accumulated: DNA는 무수한 세월에 걸쳐 축적(accumulated)된 것이지 파괴(destroyed)된 것이 아닙니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① penned: 썼다, 적절
✅ ② replaced: 대체되다, 적절
❌ ③ destroyed(파괴된) → accumulated(축적된): 반의어
✅ ④ blueprint: 청사진, 적절
✅ ⑤ dictator: 지배자, 적절

questions.passage: DNA was slowly blended and accumulated by the most <u>pitiless</u> of all phenomena.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>pitiless</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: pitiless = ruthless = 무자비한.
det.analysis:
✅ ruthless(무자비한): pitiless의 동의어
❌ optimistic(낙관적): 무관
❌ sympathetic(동정적): 반의어
❌ generous(관대한): 반의어
❌ benevolent(자비로운): 반의어

questions.passage: DNA was slowly blended and <u>accumulated</u> over countless eons.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>accumulated</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: accumulated = gathered = 축적된, 모인.
det.analysis:
✅ gathered(모은): accumulated의 동의어
❌ destroyed(파괴된): 반의어
❌ created(창조된): 다른 의미
❌ reduced(줄어든): 반의어
❌ scattered(흩어진): 반의어

questions.passage: the most <u>pitiless</u> of all phenomena — natural selection.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 pitiless와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: pitiless(무자비한) ↔ compassionate(자비로운).
det.analysis:
✅ compassionate(자비로운): pitiless의 반의어
❌ cruel(잔인한): pitiless의 유의어
❌ harsh(혹독한): pitiless의 유의어
❌ severe(가혹한): pitiless의 유의어
❌ relentless(냉혹한): pitiless의 유의어

questions.passage: “People are <u>trapped</u> in history, and history is trapped in them.”
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 trapped와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: trapped(갇힌) ↔ liberated(해방된).
det.analysis:
✅ liberated(해방된): trapped의 정확한 반의어
❌ confined(갇힌): trapped의 유의어

questions.passage: DNA is a history that is inside us — and yet one that is our master as well, the __________ for our bodies, and dictator of what we will pass on to our children.

❌ 울타리를 세웠다: pen(우리)에서 파생
❌ 가두었다: penned in의 의미
❌ 고정시켰다: 무관
det.tip: pen(명사: 펜) → pen(동사: 쓰다) → penned(과거형: 썼다)

questions.passage: each strand of DNA is an ancient record of __________ (biology) history, written in simple code.

biology → biological: 명사 → 형용사
명사 수식 → 형용사 필요

questions.passage: DNA was slowly blended and accumulated by the most __________ (pity) of all phenomena — natural selection.

det.korean: 가장 무자비한 현상 = 자연선택(natural selection).

❌ genetic engineering: 현대 기술
❌ random mutation: 무작위 돌연변이
❌ artificial selection: 인위적 선택
❌ gene therapy: 현대 의학
det.tip: natural selection = 자연선택 (다윈의 진화론 핵심 개념)

questions.passage: We are indeed trapped in this particular __________ of history as much as it is trapped in us.

det.tip: vehicle of history = 역사의 운반체 (DNA를 비유적으로 표현)

questions.passage: DNA is the dictator of what we will pass on to our children, gifts that can be blessings — or deadly __________.

❌ rewards: 축복과 유사
